This low valuation occurs alongside a market capitalisation of ₹ 694 Cr and a book value of ₹ 190 per share against a share price of ₹ 174 [E1, E2]. Crucially, the business is already showing operational green shoots through sequential momentum, evidenced by sales rising quarter-over-quarter and earnings growth accelerating [E55, E56]. This internal recovery sits within a strong industry backdrop where sector median sales growth is 17.9% and median profit growth reaches 34.0%, providing a supportive external tailwind for a turnaround [E64, E65]. This collapse in profitability is not a temporary blip, but is underscored by a negative Return on Equity of -10.03% and a negative Return on Assets of -3.9%, both of which lag far behind their respective sector benchmarks of 7.72% and 4.41% [E7, E8]. Consequently, the company's valuation of a -9.11x P/E ratio starkly highlights an unprofitable enterprise operating at a massive discount to a sector benchmark of 21.02x [E5]. Furthermore, despite the stock sitting near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 9% of its span, price growth has absurdly exceeded profit growth by 839%, indicating that market expectations are wildly detached from underlying financial reality [E4, E46]. This operational turnaround is occurring against a robust backdrop where sector median sales growth stands at 17.9% and sector median profit growth reaches 34.0% [E64, E65], providing the ideal rising tide for Heranba's recovery.
